sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the northeastern corner of the residential grid of North Plainfield, in the bend of Green Brook opposite the City of Plainfield. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. Westervelt Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Watchung Avenue along the bottom; between them run Jackson Avenue, Manning Avenue and the short Race street, with Chatham street along the right-hand side. At the top right, Brook Avenue leaves Westervelt Avenue on a diagonal beside Green Brook and meets Chatham at Elm Place. The brook itself is drawn in the top right corner, lettered with the boundary between the Borough of North Plainfield and the City of Plainfield. The two long blocks between Jackson and Manning Avenues are lined with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, with small stables, sheds and automobile houses at the rear. The large block between Manning Avenue and Chatham is taken up mostly by the Presbyterian Cemetery, which is drawn as open ground, with a row of houses along Watchung Avenue and a few along Manning Avenue and Race. Pinewood Sanitarium stands in grounds at the top of the Jackson to Manning block next to Westervelt Avenue, and a brick garage and an electric motor grain house stand at the corner of Race and Watchung Avenue. Pearl Street, Warren Street and Harmony Street appear only as stubs at the right and bottom edges, where the adjoining sheets take over.
notes: Chatham (Chatham Street) north of Watchung Avenue is today part of Brook Avenue in OpenStreetMap (Brook Avenue / Elm Place, Brook Avenue / Pearl Street).
Map, 50 ft. Jackson Av, Manning Av, Race, Chatham (today Brook Av north of Watchung Av), Brook Av, between Westervelt Av and Watchung Av; Presbyterian Cemetery; Green Brook at top right. One part.

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10 shows the blocks of North Plainfield between Watchung Avenue at the top and Somerset Street at the bottom, from Jackson Avenue on the left to Chatham Street on the right, with Manning Avenue, Race Street and Harmony Street between them. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and is separated from the lower part of the sheet by a heavy line just below Somerset Street, where the stubs of Park Place, Lincoln Place and Somerset Place lead off to sheet 18. The block between Jackson and Manning Avenues holds St. Joseph's Roman Catholic Church with its rectory and convent at the Watchung Avenue end, and a row of frame dwellings and a boarding house along both streets. The blocks further right are mostly two-storey dwellings set on narrow lots, with a paint shop on Manning Avenue and a printing office near Chatham Street. Commercial buildings line the Somerset Street frontage: a livery stable and printing shop at Manning Avenue, a bottling works, the brick Turn Hall with its stage and a bakery between Race and Harmony Streets, a pool room, and the Hotel Chatham at the corner of Chatham Street. Warren Street appears as a stub at the right edge beside Chatham Street.
notes: Turn Hall, St. Joseph's R.C. Church and Hotel Chatham are on this part.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Jackson Av to Chatham St between Watchung Av and Somerset St (north to upper left); part 2 below the line, Jackson Av to Manning Av, Westervelt Av to Norwood Av (north to upper right, from another district). Franklin Av is not in OpenStreetMap; part 2 has 3 detected points plus a hand-picked Delacy Av / Jackson Av.

sheet-10-2.description: The lower part of sheet 10, below a heavy dividing line, shows a separate district of North Plainfield several blocks north of the main part: Jackson Avenue across the top and Manning Avenue across the bottom, from Westervelt Avenue at the left edge past Franklin Avenue to Norwood Avenue at the right edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, like the rest of the sheet, but turned so that north points to the upper right. DeLacy Avenue appears only as a short stub above Jackson Avenue, in a strip referring to sheet 50. Development is sparse. The large block between Westervelt and Franklin Avenues holds the Children's Home, a large frame building near Jackson Avenue, and a scattering of dwellings and small outbuildings along Manning Avenue; much of the block is open ground divided into lots. East of Franklin Avenue, Jackson Avenue is marked as not open, and the block toward Norwood Avenue is occupied by the greenhouses of Brooks Carson, florist, drawn as a group of long glass houses with a heating plant, together with a dwelling. Fire hydrants and water pipes are marked along Westervelt and Manning Avenues.
notes: Jackson Avenue east of Franklin Avenue is marked 'Not Open'.
Franklin Avenue has no junction in OpenStreetMap here; the part is placed from three detected junctions and a hand-picked DeLacy Avenue / Jackson Avenue.
Greenhouses of Brooks Carson, florist.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Jackson Av to Chatham St between Watchung Av and Somerset St (north to upper left); part 2 below the line, Jackson Av to Manning Av, Westervelt Av to Norwood Av (north to upper right, from another district). Franklin Av is not in OpenStreetMap; part 2 has 3 detected points plus a hand-picked Delacy Av / Jackson Av.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the centre of North Plainfield along Somerset Street, the borough's main street, which runs down the right-hand side of the sheet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Grove, Duer and Vine run down the sheet between Park Place at the top and Craig Place at the bottom, crossed by Mercer Avenue, Lincoln Place and Somerset Place. The Somerset Street frontage is the commercial and civic core: Somerset High School with its manual training building fills the top right block, followed by an ice cream factory, stores, the Fire Department house of Engine Company No. 1, the Somerset Hotel, the police station with paints and oils stores, and at Somerset Place the warehouse of the Hand Storage and Express Company, with a livery stable behind it. The rest of the sheet is residential: frame dwellings of two to three storeys on Grove, Duer and Vine, with sheds, stables and automobile houses behind, and St. Peter's Swedish Lutheran Church on Mercer Avenue. A table of the fire department's men and apparatus is printed in the right margin. Cross streets on the far side of Somerset Street (Jackson Avenue, Manning Avenue, Race Street, Harmony Street, Chatham Street and Pearl Street) are shown as stubs, and Prospect Place appears at the lower left.
notes: Somerset High School, Fire Department Engine Co. No. 1, police station, Somerset Hotel, Hand Storage and Express Co. warehouse.
Fire department table in the right margin (left out of the mask).
Map, 50 ft (pilot). Grove, Duer, Vine, Somerset between Park Pl and Craig Pl; Somerset High School, fire house, police station. One part; fire department table in the right margin notched out.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers three residential blocks of North Plainfield between Somerset Street on the left and Watchung Avenue on the right, from Codington Avenue at the top past Regent and Mountain Avenue to Summit Avenue at the bottom edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. The top edge also shows the bottom of the block above Codington Avenue, part of sheet 50. The blocks are divided into regular lots and built up with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, a few of brick, with stables, carriage houses, sheds, coops and automobile houses at the rear; the middle block holds a group of carriage houses and stables near its centre. Much of the block between Mountain and Summit Avenues is still open, with a row of small dwellings at the Somerset Street end and new houses facing Summit Avenue. Streets entering from the other side of Somerset Street are shown as stubs: Dupont Street at Codington Avenue, Union Street opposite Regent, and Green Brook Road near the bottom left. Water pipes of six and eight inches are marked along the streets, and the street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at the corners. A scale of feet is printed in Mountain Avenue.
notes: Green Brook Road is today Greenbrook Road.
Map, 50 ft. Somerset to Watchung Av, Codington Av to Summit Av. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 continues the residential district of North Plainfield south of sheet 19, between Somerset Street on the left and Watchung Avenue on the right, from Summit Avenue at the top past Grandview and Fairview Avenues to Jackson Avenue at the bottom edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Allen Place runs into the middle block from Fairview Avenue and ends partway to Grandview Avenue. All three blocks are divided into narrow lots and built up with frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, with stables, sheds, carriage houses and automobile houses behind; there is a dairy behind the Grandview Avenue houses near Allen Place, two stores near Somerset Street at Grandview Avenue, and a few vacant outbuildings. The block between Fairview and Jackson Avenues is less closely built, with several open lots along Somerset Street. Linden Avenue enters from the far side of Somerset Street as a stub. The left margin carries the number of sheet 22 and the right margin that of sheet 50, which draw the adjoining blocks. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets, with street widths of 50 and 60 feet, and a scale of feet is printed in the lower right corner.
notes: Map, 50 ft. Somerset to Watchung Av, Summit Av to Jackson Av, Allen Pl. One part.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows the part of North Plainfield west of Somerset Street, between Dupont at the top and Green Brook Road, which crosses the lower part of the sheet on a diagonal. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Grove, Duer and Stone run down the sheet, with Somerset along the right-hand edge; Steiner Place leaves Dupont at the top and Union crosses from Stone to Somerset. Large blocks between Grove and Duer are still largely undeveloped, divided into long lots with only a few dwellings at the Dupont end. Between Duer and Stone and along Somerset the lots are smaller and built up with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys; a stone outbuilding and a bakery with ovens stand behind the Somerset frontage. Below Green Brook Road the blocks are more mixed: dwellings along Grove and Duer, a store, a liquor store, a bottling house and stables, and a large building at the Somerset corner. Dupont at the top edge is drawn only to the line of its blocks. Water pipes and hydrants are marked, with street widths of 50 and 60 feet, and a scale of feet is printed near the bottom.
notes: Green Brook Road (printed Green Brook R'd) is today Greenbrook Road.
Dupont (Dupont Street) junctions were hand-picked 25 ft beyond the drawn block line.

Map, 50 ft. Grove, Duer, Stone, Somerset between Dupont St and Green Brook Rd (today Greenbrook Road). One part. Dupont St at the top edge is drawn only to its block lines: the detector put its junctions about 15 m inside the blocks (scale 7.66 px/ft), so they are excluded and hand-picked 25 ft beyond the block line.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 lies below sheet 21 in North Plainfield, between Grove Street on the left and Somerset Street on the right, from the blocks south of Green Brook Road at the top to Park Place at the bottom, crossed by Linden Avenue. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Duer runs down the middle and Steiner Place runs from Linden Avenue up into the block above, where it ends. Rockview Avenue enters from the left as a stub opposite the Grove frontage, and Park Place is lettered again at the lower left. The long blocks along Grove and Duer are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots. Between Duer and Steiner Place stands the R. H. McCullough sash and blind factory, with a lumber shed and drying room, and between Steiner Place and Somerset the W. J. Conroy carriage factory with a painting shop, repository and harness room, together with bowling alleys and a saloon on the Somerset frontage. Grace Methodist Episcopal Church stands at the corner of Park Place and Somerset. The rest of the lower blocks hold dwellings and a few stables and storage buildings. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets, and a scale of feet is printed in Park Place at the bottom right.
notes: R. H. McCullough sash and blind factory; W. J. Conroy carriage factory; Grace M.E. Church.
Map, 50 ft. Grove, Duer, Steiner Pl, Somerset between Green Brook Rd area and Park Pl; R.H. McCullough sash factory, W.J. Conroy carriage factory, Grace M.E. Church. One part.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 shows the business centre of Plainfield on the south side of Green Brook, although the sheet is headed North Plainfield. It covers the long block between West Front Street on the left and West 2nd Street on the right, from Park Avenue at the top to Central Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Madison Avenue, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. Somerset Street and East Front Street enter at the top left where Front Street widens at Park Avenue, and Grove Street meets Front Street at Central Avenue. The Front Street frontage is solidly built with brick stores of two to four storeys, many with offices or dwellings above, and bakeries, drug stores and a laundry among them. Behind them stand the Plainfield Theatre and Elks Hall near Park Avenue, Trinity Reformed Church, the house of Fire Department Engine Company No. 1 on Exchange Alley, the Allen Pharmacal Company, St. Stephan's ice cream factory, Frank Linke's bottling works, the Plainfield Nickle Plate Company and the Plainfield Wagon Manufacturing Company. Prudens Alley and Exchange Alley cross the upper block. Below Madison Avenue are the First Methodist Episcopal Church, automobile supply stores, Calvary Baptist Church and Reform Hall. Dwellings are found mainly along West 2nd Street.
notes: Although headed North Plainfield, the sheet shows the City of Plainfield (Union County) south of Green Brook.

Somerset Street met Front Street about 30 m south of Park Avenue; today the junction of Park Avenue, Somerset Street and Front Street is one node, about 25 m from the drawn Park Avenue / West Front junction, and was not used.

Map, 50 ft. Headed North Plainfield but drawn in the City of Plainfield (Union County): W. Front St to W. 2nd St between Park Av and Central Av, downtown commercial. One part. Park Av / W Front St modern node (also Somerset St) is about 25 m off the drawn junction and is not used; Park Av / W 2nd St hand-picked.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 shows the western residential section of North Plainfield, a district of curving streets between Stony Brook at the top and Green Brook, the boundary with the City of Plainfield, at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Rockview Terrace and Rockview Avenue sweep across the upper half of the sheet, with Linden Avenue, Park Place, Mercer Avenue and Willow Avenue following the curve below them; Sycamore Avenue, Orchard Avenue and Washington Avenue cut across, and Myrtle Avenue and Prospect Place run near the bottom. Grove Street runs along the right edge and Geraud Avenue down the left edge. The district is laid out in large irregular lots with detached frame dwellings, some of brick, many with automobile houses. A pond fed by a small stream lies in the open ground at the top left, beside an estate with outbuildings, and a large house in grounds stands between Rockview and Linden Avenues. The Church of the Holy Cross with its chapel stands on Washington Avenue near Grove Street, and a large institutional building is drawn at the bottom where Washington Avenue reaches Green Brook. Large open lots lie along Geraud Avenue. The brook is lettered with the names of the Borough of North Plainfield and the City of Plainfield.
notes: Church of the Holy Cross on Washington Avenue.
Map, 100 ft. Rockview Av, Mercer Av, Sycamore Av, Washington Av to Grove St, Willow Av, Myrtle Av, Geraud Av; Stony Brook and Green Brook (borough line with the City of Plainfield). One part.

sheet-50-1.description: The main part of sheet 50 shows the northern residential district of North Plainfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. Watchung Avenue runs along the left edge, and Verdon, Whitewood Avenue, Westervelt Avenue, DeLacy Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Norwood Avenue run down the sheet; Codington Avenue, Regent, Mountain Avenue, Summit Avenue, Grandview Avenue, Fairview Avenue and Jackson Avenue cross them. Almont Place is a short street off Fairview Avenue. The western blocks, between Watchung and Westervelt Avenues, are divided into narrow lots and well built up with frame dwellings, with the Watchung School at Watchung Avenue below Regent, Warren Chapel at the corner of Watchung and Fairview Avenues, and a woodworking shop on Whitewood Avenue. East of Westervelt Avenue the land is a newer subdivision: the blocks between DeLacy, Franklin and Norwood Avenues are drawn as long rows of empty lots numbered 136 to 140, with only a few dwellings along DeLacy Avenue. The top right of the sheet is taken by an inset in a heavy box (part 2), and the stub of the block above Codington Avenue is drawn at the top. Water pipes and hydrants are marked, and a scale of feet is printed in Jackson Avenue.
notes: Verdon is today Verdon Street; Regent is Regent Street.
Watchung School; Warren Chapel.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map, Watchung Av to Norwood Av between Codington Av and Jackson Av; part 2 inset in a heavy box at top right, Somerset St from Hudson Av to Dupont St with Fritz Pl, Howard St and Steiner Pl, drawn with north to the upper left.

sheet-50-2.description: The inset in the heavy box at the top right of sheet 50 shows a short stretch of Somerset Street in North Plainfield, north of the area of sheet 21, from Hudson Avenue and Fritz Place past Howard Street to Dupont Street, with Steiner Place along the bottom of the inset. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, like the main part, but turned so that north points to the upper left, with its own north arrow. Somerset Street runs across the top. The block between Fritz Place and Howard Street is mostly open, with a row of dwellings along Fritz Place and a few along Howard Street and Somerset Street. Between Howard Street and Dupont, above Steiner Place, stand the long glass houses of a greenhouse establishment with a dwelling and a shed. Below Steiner Place a further block, numbered 21, is outlined with one dwelling. The margins of the inset carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 19, 21, 24 and 130, and the block numbers 23 and 20. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Somerset Street, and the street widths of 50 feet are lettered at the corners.
notes: Inset drawn with north to the upper left, about 90 degrees from the main part.
Greenhouses between Howard Street and Dupont Street.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map, Watchung Av to Norwood Av between Codington Av and Jackson Av; part 2 inset in a heavy box at top right, Somerset St from Hudson Av to Dupont St with Fritz Pl, Howard St and Steiner Pl, drawn with north to the upper left.
